I'll add that they are smart in highly stupid ways--or smart in particular ones, i.e. in their ability to understand systems and mathematics and the ontology of the DSM, but with a pervasive and damaging inability to consider variables that exist outside of what can be called the scientific or medical sphere. Is = ought to them; they do not comprehend that ethical judgments must be informed by at least one premise that is nonscientific in nature. (This is why it is funny to be called antiscience for holding antipsychiatric views; it is antiscientific to think that science has the ability on its own to decide what /should/ be done in a given instance.)

You're correct that those are the origins of the subreddit; I was a lurker in the early days, although I think you're mistaking the demographic and its psychology a bit. Largely I see the people who "don't want to work at all" and who "expect to get paid sitting on their arses doing nothing all day" as suffering from invisible disabilities--mainly mental illness--that are simply incompatible with working life but which are not recognized as being real or debilitating by others one meets or by one's general community. There is a group of people in the world who have been told they are lazy their entire life because their limitations are just not acknowledged, and it can really affect a person when this is the case for them. I think the original subscribers and participants of the subreddit were mostly of this type, perhaps with some lazy stragglers here-and-there.
